CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Judy Gomez is a patient with psoriatic arthritis presenting for routine follow-up. She reports good control on prednisone 1 mg daily, which represents a successful dose reduction from previous visits. She occasionally required an extra dose approximately once weekly due to mild foot pain, particularly on days with increased activity related to her desk job. She reports significant improvement in joint pain since initiation of methotrexate. She held methotrexate during her first COVID-19 vaccine dose due to concerns about vaccine efficacy but experienced severe pain during that week. She resumed methotrexate for the second vaccine dose per telephone hotline guidance. She reports easy bruising without associated trauma or sensation, which she notes appears spontaneously.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain in foot joints and some discomfort in knee joints, though knee pain has improved since methotrexate dose increase. She notes easy bruising without preceding trauma. No other systemic symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (to be discontinued).
Methotrexate (dose recently increased, patient tolerating well).

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job. She remains active on days off.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient alert and cooperative.
Extremities: Feet and toe joints examined. Good range of motion in toes. Ridges noted in nails consistent with psoriasis. Knee flexion pain-free. No acute distress with joint manipulation.

RESULTS
Blood work pending; appointment to be scheduled at front desk.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis on methotrexate with good response. Discontinue prednisone today. Easy bruising likely related to prednisone; expect improvement with discontinuation. Schedule blood work appointment at front desk for methotrexate monitoring. Follow-up visit in three months.
